heuristic.applicability: Prefer after approach when fingers are closing/closed and the agent is uncertain whether to keep extracting/lifting or begin transfer, provided object/world tunnel geometry is near training support and target_pose is the intended drawer destination. It is also valid from the shared 300:440 entry overlap, but its principal benefit is 540:840 ordering. Inputs must show finite object, TCP, finger and destination states.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer is open/stable; block is low in the tunnel; target_pose is the intended drawer destination; gripper is open at normal entry or closed only when TCP remains near a plausibly held block.
handoff.exit_conditions: Observed object is outside the tunnel, above 0.16 m, moving with TCP under closed fingers, and destination-relative commands have begun transfer toward the open drawer.
handoff.failure_signatures: Closed fingers without object/TCP coupling, guard repeatedly projecting requested +x motion while object remains low, object failing to rise, destination-relative drift, object drop, or persistent IK nonconvergence/limit contact.
handoff.overlap_role: All actions 300:840 remain supervised. The 300:440 overlap supports starts during retreat/approach; 680:840 teaches the clearance/reorientation/transfer transition shared with placement.
handoff.successor_readiness: Guard becomes inactive after observed clearance. Hand off during 680:840 once coupled object/TCP motion persists above clearance and destination-directed transfer has begun.

heuristic.limitations: The guard uses finger proximity/motion proxies because contact truth is unavailable; it can be fooled by a closed but empty gripper and cannot retry a failed grasp. It does not prove collision freedom or success. Destination anchoring is sensitive to large block displacement and changed tunnel pose; choose the object-frame prior for reliable displaced blocks. Absolute destination-frame targets can be brittle to unusual predecessor TCP configurations; choose the fresh-TCP delta prior for that case. The guard may reject a valid unseen maneuver that intentionally transfers below clearance.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Inputs contain two causal frames of robot state, destination-relative and object-relative transforms, gripper width, object/TCP motion-coupling features, and signed tunnel/clearance margins. Learned actions are 10-D destination-frame translation (metres), destination-frame 6-D rotation, and gripper scalar. encode_targets composes inverse(pre-action target_pose) with commanded FK TCP. decode_action resolves the current target_pose, composes the world target, applies only the declared low-clearance guard, and calls verified IK from fresh qpos, reporting projection and IK diagnostics. The mature standard backbone and fixed recipe are unchanged.
heuristic.rationale: The successful sequence has a strict geometric ordering: align at low z near 0.089 (520:540), close and pull outward in -x while the object remains near z 0.08 (560:600), lift (620:700) past the 0.16 roof, then reorient and move toward the drawer (780:840). A two-frame input exposes finger width, object/TCP relative pose, object and TCP displacement coupling, tunnel margins and clearance margin rather than asking the backbone to infer all phase cues from raw state. Destination-relative absolute targets retain world tunnel/drawer structure and resist drift during the long transfer. The decoder guard only intervenes when fingers are closed, TCP is near the observed block, block z is below the supplied clearance, and a sample asks for premature +x drawer transfer; demonstrated low extraction is in -x, so labels remain valid. This aims at unsafe phase confusion, not failed-grasp recovery.
heuristic.statement: Destination-frame geometry and clearance prior: diffuse absolute TCP poses relative to target_pose, condition on explicit two-frame grasp/coupling and tunnel-margin features, and apply a narrow deterministic guard that forbids a closed-near-object command from transferring toward the drawer before the observed block clears z=0.16. Prefer it when closure/lift/transfer phase is ambiguous but block and tunnel remain near demonstrated world geometry.

assignment.subgoal: With the drawer already open, move from the drawer-retreat state to the tunnel, descend within the tunnel clearance, align an open gripper around the block, close on it, pull it horizontally out of the tunnel, then lift it above the 0.16 m tunnel clearance and begin transfer toward the drawer. Approximate entry: drawer open and stable, block low near z=0.08, gripper open. Approximate exit: block held with closed fingers and elevated around z=0.30-0.32 or higher, outside the tunnel and moving toward the drawer.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: Destination-frame encode/decode must recover demonstrated FK TCP and gripper within 0.01 maximum metres/radians/scalar. The declared guard is inactive on valid demonstrated targets; any projection and all IK residuals are reported.

contract.cut_relation: Keeps all [300,840) actions for each trajectory, including [300,440) predecessor and [680,840) successor overlap. The only nonlearned refinement is the declared low-clearance projection; it does not add task waypoints.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is [destination-frame TCP x,y,z metres, destination-frame TCP rotation 6D as first two columns, gripper scalar]. decode composes the represented pose with the freshly observed target_pose. If and only if observed fingers are closed, TCP is within 0.06 m of the block and block z is below tunnel_clearance_m, a deterministic projection caps premature +world-x transfer to object_x+0.03 m and keeps y inside the object-centre tunnel lane while the block is inside tunnel x. Rotation is unchanged. The resulting world TCP pose goes through panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh joints. Gripper >=0 opens and <0 closes. Slots are t-1..t+14; execution uses 1..8.
contract.parameter_semantics: object_pose_field selects the observed manipulated block used for proximity, motion and clearance features; destination_pose_field selects the observed SE(3) frame for learned targets; tunnel_clearance_m is world z=0.16 m and enters both features and the conservative decoder guard. Bindings use object_pose, target_pose and 0.16.
